newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds finished slightly firmer in quiet trading but hardly reacted to generally positive news from the summit of European Union (EU) leaders here.
Dealers and brokers reported interested in all parts of the guilder yield curve except for medium-term maturities.
On the first day of their two-day meeting, EU ministers agreed on a pact linking budget discipline among member nations adopting a single currency to economic growth and jobs.
The yield on the 10-year benchmark, the 5.75 percent February 2007 bond, closed at 5.55 percent, one basis point below the level of Friday's end.
One dealer expressed surprise that the stability pact agreement, the precise details of which have not been divulged, had little impact on the domestic market.
He said the announcement may have been expected in view of the new Leftist French government's insistence that any deal include a commitment to job creation.
"What's more important is what's actually in it," he said.
The dealer said it was a political market which could move in any direction, adding that a "softer" Euro currency was discounted in prices.
One trader said interest in the February 2007 bonds may be rekindled from June 24, the day after payment for the recently issued second tranche of the benchmark.
Another dealer noted a small up-tick in guilder bond prices on news of the deal. "It was more or less expected," he said.

He said Tuesday would bring May inflation, housing and production data from the United States, where the consensus seems to be that the Federal Reserve is unlikely to lift interest rates at its July 1/2 meeting. "Then we can see whether this optimistic mood can be maintained," he said.
